# Input and Output Checklist: Basic Arithmetic

**Purpose**: Test whether the spec's requirements for input, errors, and output are complete, clear, and consistent, before tasks are written. Each item asks about the spec's wording, not about code.
**Created**: 2026-11-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Markers in brackets: the quality being tested (Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Coverage), the requirement it concerns, and `Gap` when the spec may be missing something.

## Number Format

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec say whether a number may start with `+` (for example `+5 + 3`), or that only `-` is allowed as a sign? [Clarity, [FR-003](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec say that a number cannot start or end with the decimal point (`.5`, `5.`), with an edge case for each? [Coverage, [FR-003](../spec.md#functional-requirements), [Edge Cases](../spec.md#edge-cases)]
- [x] CHK003 Is it clear that the `-` sign does not count toward the 3-digit limit (`-999` is valid)? [Clarity, [FR-014](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK004 Does the spec say whether `-0` and `0.00` are valid numbers, and that dividing by either counts as division by zero? [Coverage, [FR-003](../spec.md#functional-requirements), [FR-007](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec say whether a tab counts as a space, since [FR-001](../spec.md#functional-requirements) only mentions spaces? [Clarity, Gap]

## Error Messages and Their Order

- [x] CHK006 Does [FR-005](../spec.md#functional-requirements)'s list of shape problems (missing number, extra input, unknown operator) match the six shape messages in the [Error messages](../spec.md#error-messages) table (which adds nothing entered, missing operator, and operator not between the numbers)? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK007 Is the rule for choosing one shape message when several could apply (for example `4 x 2`: unknown operator or not a number?) written in the spec? Today it is only in [R5](../research.md#r5--finding-mistakes-in-the-input), but the user sees the result. [Gap, Consistency]
- [x] CHK008 Is it specified that a `-` joined to a word that is not a number (`-abc + 3`) is reported as `"-abc" is not a number`, not as a shape problem? Today this is only in [R5](../research.md#r5--finding-mistakes-in-the-input). [Gap, [FR-001](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK009 Is it clear whether division by zero is still reported when the right number also breaks the digit limit (for example `5 / 0.000`)? [FR-015](../spec.md#functional-requirements) only stops further checks for numbers that are not numbers. [Clarity, Gap]
- [x] CHK010 Is it clear how `<text>` is shown in a message when the typed text itself contains double quotes (for example `"5" + 3`)? [Clarity, [Error messages](../spec.md#error-messages)]
- [x] CHK011 Does every message in the [Error messages](../spec.md#error-messages) table name the problem, the offending text where there is one, and what is accepted, as [NFR-002](../spec.md#non-functional-requirements) requires? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK012 Is the order of messages for a number with several problems (leading zeros and too many digits, as in `0999`) defined without doubt? [Clarity, [FR-015](../spec.md#functional-requirements), [Edge Cases](../spec.md#edge-cases)]

## Result Format

- [x] CHK013 Are rounding, removal of trailing zeros, and "never `-0`" in [FR-004](../spec.md#functional-requirements) each backed by at least one example in the spec? [Coverage]
- [x] CHK014 Is it clear that results have no thousands separator (`1998`, not `1,998`), given that input like `1,000` is rejected? [Clarity, [FR-004](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]

## One-shot Mode

- [x] CHK015 Does the spec say where results and errors appear in one-shot mode, or point to the plan, now that [R3](../research.md#r3--where-output-goes-in-one-shot-mode) and [R4](../research.md#r4--how-a-script-knows-whether-the-operation-worked) have decided it? The spec's [Assumptions](../spec.md#assumptions) still say "left to the plan". [Consistency, [FR-011](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK016 Is it specified what happens when one-shot mode is given `quit`, `exit`, or an empty argument (`calc ""`)? [Coverage, [FR-011](../spec.md#functional-requirements), [FR-013](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]

## Interactive Session

- [x] CHK017 Does the spec say what happens when input is piped in with no operation argument (for example `echo "2+3" | calc`): an interactive session with the welcome message and prompts, or something else? [Coverage, Gap, [FR-012](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK018 Is it clear what the session prints when it ends (nothing, or a goodbye line), for `quit`, `exit`, and end of input? [Clarity, [FR-013](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK019 Is it clear whether a line that only contains spaces counts as blank (ignored) or as an empty operation (error)? [Clarity, [FR-013](../spec.md#functional-requirements)]
- [x] CHK020 Do [US4](../spec.md#us4--one-shot-and-interactive-modes-p4) criteria 1 and 4 show the same layout as [FR-012](../spec.md#functional-requirements) (answer, 59-character separator, prompt)? [Consistency]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK021 Does every acceptance criterion in [US1](../spec.md#us1--compute-a-basic-operation-p1) to [US4](../spec.md#us4--one-shot-and-interactive-modes-p4) name its mode where the output differs between modes? [Clarity]
- [x] CHK022 Can every acceptance criterion and edge case be checked by comparing exact text, with no criterion that needs a person's judgment? [Measurability, [Definition of Done](../spec.md#definition-of-done)]
